name: Lundenwic
status: trial: a first config to prove the thames_793 source; the anchors, the clearing and the water level want the place's own research
about: The strand market on the Thames c. 800 (Lundenwic, the Strand), at true size
centre_about: British National Grid: the Strand's reach of the Thames, the port a little north-east of the centre

rivers.name: Thames
rivers.about: thames_793's class 3 (the channel and its creeks); the carve makes it at least 3.5 m under the mean level mid-river, the raster's own bed kept where deeper

tide.about: High water +1.25 m ODN (thames_793.py's HW_793: archaeological estimates for London's Saxon waterfront +1.0..+1.5); the mean range c. 800 2.4 m (springs 3.0) from Research/water_levels/north_sea_core.json thames_lundenwic, which marks it a guess (low confidence). Low water = high water - range.

water_level.about: the mean of the tide's high and low water: the level's base, the tide moves the water round it

shore.about: no bank lift: the tidal shore is the raster's own foreshore

outer.about: the EA LIDAR Composite DTM 2022 of today, 70 m median (the raster's own rule for ground kept)

settlement.about: the Strand settlement, about 1.4 km along the river centred on the port, on the north bank (a guess)

clearings.label: Lundenburh's clearing (the walled Roman city: the minster and open ground)
clearings.about: level metres: St Paul's (BNG 532000, 181130); a guess

cover_names.1: terrace edge and dry bank: the high dry ground by the river (settlement, fields, hay)
cover_names.7: gravel terrace: dry old high ground away from the river (fields, oak and hazel on the driest parts)

sources: The tidal Thames c. 793 from the EA LIDAR Composite DTM 2022 (Contains Environment Agency information (c) Environment Agency and/or database right 2022, OGL v3), the first build's Bake/realground/thames_793.py
Today's ground beyond the floodplain: the same EA LIDAR Composite DTM 2022 (OGL v3)
Allen, G. H. & Pavelsky, T. M. (2018), Global extent of rivers and streams, Science 361 (GRWL, CC BY 4.0): the channel's centre line
